**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 24 (Assignment and Change of Control) already delivers our preferred position on all four elements:

- **24.1** — Customer may assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets (prompt notice + assignee assumption, which is acceptable).
- **24.2** — Vendor may not assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld for a capable, financially sound assignee), and never to a direct Customer competitor.
- **24.3** — Residual assignments are governed by a mutual, reasonableness-qualified consent standard.
- **24.4** — Expressly negates any Vendor right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, and requires Vendor cooperation with successor administrative changes.

I also checked for residual or conflicting language: a document-wide search for "assign" and "change of control" surfaced nothing adverse. Section 9 termination is limited to insolvency-type events (no change-of-control trigger), Section 13 confirms our licence rights transfer with a Section 24-permitted assignment, and Section 30.5 preserves enforcement rights for permitted successors and Customer Affiliates. Walk-away risks (blanket bar on our assignment, or a Vendor exit/re-pricing right on our change of control) are absent.
